title: DRV Book I  -  The Lock  -  REWRITE v2 (Phase 4.1 III)

canonical_node.axiom: The argument from properties of mathematical truth to the Logos is structured in six layers with distinct epistemic statuses, terminating at the Feb 14 floor: Axiom 1 (God-as-Axiom) as the first primitive axiom, with Axioms 2 and 3 acknowledged.
definitions: Layer 0: Properties of Truth (P0.1 - P0.7) are below-floor presuppositions, not axioms.
Layer 1: Gdel-Chaitin Theorem is an external inherited result, not an axiom.
Layer 2: Inferences 2.1 - 2.3 are derivations from Theorem 1.
Layer 3: Source-Property Transmission Lemma is a single inference replacing four prior axioms.
Layer 4: Definitions 4.1 - 4.2 are definitions and theological postulates.
Layer 5: Central Claim is the thesis defended, not an axiom.
Layer 6: Definition 6.1 names the ground 'Logos'; Axiom 1 identifies it as God-as-Axiom.
derivation: Layer 0: Seven properties of mathematical truth are observed as below-floor presuppositions.
Layer 1: Gdel-Chaitin theorem establishes the ground of mathematical truth is external to mathematics.
Layer 2: From the theorem, the ground cannot be nothing, chaos, or deceptive.
Layer 3: The Source-Property Transmission Lemma transfers properties from truth to the ground.
Layer 4: Definitions and postulates about truth's value and deception's wrongness are adopted.
Layer 5: The Central Claim asserts math and moral truth share a single ground.
Layer 6: The ground is named Logos and identified as Axiom 1 (God-as-Axiom).
canonical_node.action: The system should treat the III argument as a layered structure with distinct epistemic statuses, not as a flat set of twenty axioms. It should recognize Axiom 1 as the foundational primitive, with Axioms 2 and 3 acknowledged but not load-bearing in this series.
boundary: Does not assert the seven properties as axioms; they are below-floor presuppositions.
Does not treat Gdel-Chaitin as an axiom of the framework; it is an external theorem.
Does not treat the Central Claim as an axiom; it is the thesis defended.
Does not push beyond the Feb 14 floor into divine mechanics.
Does not exercise Axiom 2 (Trinity Isomorphism) in this series.
test: Verify that each layer's epistemic status matches the taxonomy (below-floor, external theorem, derivation, lemma, definition, central claim, axiom).
Check that the argument terminates at the Feb 14 floor without descending below it.
Confirm that Axiom 1 is the first primitive axiom and Axioms 2 and 3 are acknowledged appropriately.

dg1_dependencies: Gdel's Second Incompleteness and Chaitin's complexity bound
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reclassified III that distinguishes epistemic statuses of the argument steps, promoting A20 to Axiom 1 and demoting A1 - A7 to below-floor properties, enabling clearer formal grounding.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the content of the original twenty axioms while reclassifying their status; maintains the Feb 14 floor as the formal boundary.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this rewrite is removed, the framework reverts to a flat-axiom structure that misrepresents the May 10 canon, potentially undermining the formal taxonomy and the load-bearing status of Axiom 1.

overstatement_risks: The document claims the argument 'derives' the Logos, but the derivation relies on theological postulates and definitions, not formal proof.
The promotion of A20 to Axiom 1 is a reclassification, not a new proof of God's existence.
The document asserts the Gdel-Chaitin theorem 'forces' the conclusion, but the inference to a personal God is not mathematically forced.
kill_conditions: If the Formal Theory v1.0 canon is not accepted, the reclassification loses its basis.
If the Gdel-Chaitin theorem is misapplied, the argument collapses.
If the Central Claim is treated as an axiom, the framework reverts to the flat structure.
risk.lean_target: The document should be treated as a theological argument with a formal taxonomy, not as a mathematical proof of the Logos.

plain_summary: This document is a rewrite of III of DRV Book I, reclassifying the original twenty axioms into a six-layer argument with distinct epistemic statuses, culminating in Axiom 1 (God-as-Axiom) as the foundational primitive. It is a theological reclassification, not a formal proof.
